text_blocks.snippet: Smoking significantly worsens the impact of diabetes, increasing the risk of complications and making it harder to manage the condition. It can lead to a higher risk of heart disease, kidney disease, vision loss, and nerve damage. Furthermore, smoking can worsen insulin resistance and make blood sugar control more challenging.
snippet_highlighted_words: increasing the risk of complications and making it harder to manage the condition

list.snippet: Increased risk of type 2 diabetes: Smoking is a well-established risk factor for type 2 diabetes, with smokers having a 30-40% higher chance of developing the condition compared to non-smokers.
Mechanism: Smoking damages cells, causes inflammation, and interferes with insulin's effectiveness, leading to insulin resistance.
Dose-response relationship: The more cigarettes smoked, the higher the risk of developing diabetes.

list.title: Increased risk of complications:
list.snippet: Smoking worsens existing diabetes complications, such as heart disease, kidney disease, vision loss (retinopathy), and nerve damage (neuropathy).

list.title: Difficulties with insulin:
list.snippet: Smoking can make it harder to control blood sugar levels and manage diabetes, often requiring higher insulin doses.

list.title: Reduced blood circulation:
list.snippet: Smoking impairs blood circulation, which can exacerbate diabetic foot problems and increase the risk of amputation.
Insulin resistance: Smoking can make cells less responsive to insulin, leading to higher blood sugar levels.
Increased risk of cardiovascular complications: Diabetes and smoking independently increase the risk of heart attacks and strokes, and their combination further elevates these risks.
Difficulty with medication: Smoking can make it harder to manage diabetes with medication.

list.title: Improved blood sugar control:
list.snippet: Quitting smoking can improve insulin sensitivity and blood sugar control.

list.title: Reduced risk of complications:
list.snippet: Quitting smoking can significantly reduce the risk of developing diabetes complications.

list.title: Improved circulation:
list.snippet: Smoking cessation improves blood circulation, which is crucial for overall health, especially for individuals with diabetes.

list.title: Better heart health:
list.snippet: Quitting smoking can reduce the risk of heart disease and improve overall cardiovascular health.

text_blocks.snippet: Studies have shown that smokers are 30-40% more likely to develop type 2 diabetes compared to non-smokers. The risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked and the duration of smoking.

Smoking damages the body's insulin-producing cells, making it harder for the body to regulate blood sugar levels. It also increases inflammation and oxidative stress, which contribute to the development of diabetes.

Quitting smoking can significantly reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Even if a person has already been diagnosed with diabetes, quitting smoking can help improve blood sugar control and reduce the risk of complications.
